AWAR D 1.
Present claim petition has been filed u/s 140/166 of M.V. Act by the petitioners being legal heirs of deceased Rahul Kumar s/o Rajesh Kumar.
Facts in brief are that on 31.03.2022 deceased Rahul Kumar along with his brother Saurabh was going on his motorcycle to his in-laws house at Chijarshi from Meet Nagar, Delhi.

It is stated that at about 11.00 a.m. when deceased reached near Chijarshhi Toll Tax, in the meanwhile offending truck bearing registration no.UK-06CB-3469 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from behind and hit the motorcycle of the deceased,
due to which deceased fell down on the road and sustained head injury and on other parts of body and diet at the spot.
It is stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver/respondent no.1.

Regarding the accident in question, an FIR No.0128/2022 u/s 279/338/304A IPC was registered at PS Pilakhua, District Hapur, U.P.
2.

It is stated that at the time of accident deceased Rahul Kumar was doing house keeping work in Eagle Eye, Security and House Keeping Services and used to earn Rs.18,000/- per month.
3.

WS to the claim petition has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 wherein an objection has been taken that vehicle of the respondent was parked on the side of road as respondent no.1 was getting MACT No.395/2022 by SHELENDER Page 2 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.09.13 16:38:57 +0530 fresh by using toilet.

In the meantime petitioner came driving his motorcycle in a very rash and negligent manner and hit the parked vehicle of respondents, fell on the road and suddenly one another car came from back side and hit the motorcycle of petitioner.
It is stated that accident due to negligence of petitioner and vehicle of respondents has been falsely implicated.
It is pleaded that no accident took place from the vehicle of respondents.
It is stated that vehicle of respondents was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

4. Written statement has not been filed on behalf of respondent no.2.
5.
In the WS filed on behalf of insurance company/R3 an objection has been taken that accident has taken place due to sole fault, negligence of deceased himself.

It is stated that deceased was driving the vehicle without following traffic rules and in high speed which caused alleged injuries to him and said fact is clear from mechanical inspection of both the vehicles.
Insurance company has taken the defence/pleas in terms of section 147, 149, 157, 134(C), 170 of M.V. Act.

However it stated that vehicle in question was duly insured under policy no.34040331210100003288 with validity from 11.01.2022 to 10.01.2023.
6.

On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 18.10.2023 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle/truck no.UK-06CB-3469 on 31.03.2022 at 11.00 pm at near Chijarshi Toll Tax within the jurisdiction of PS Pilakhua, District Hapur, UP in a rash and negligent manner and Kajal And Ors vs Firasat Ali And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102422473/

Issue No.1 10.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: To prove the manner in which accident has occurred, PW2 Saurabh deposed that he is eye witness in the present case.
PW2 says that on 31.03.2022 he along with his cousin brother Rahul was going on different motorcycles to in-laws house at Pilakhuva, Hapur from Meet Nagar, Delhi.

Witness says that at about 11.00 p.m. when PW2 and his brother reached at Sagar Hotel, just before Chhijarsi Toll Tax, suddenly respondent no.1/driver of the offending truck bearing no.UK-06CB-3469 came by driving the truck in a very rash and negligent manner from behind and hit the motorcycle of Rahul, due to said impact Rahul received grievous head injury and died at the spot.
PW2 says that said truck was caught at the spot.
Witness states that accident has occurred due to negligent driving of truck driver as he came from behind.
14. It is submitted by the counsel for insurance that name of PW2 is not mentioned in the police charge sheet and evidence of PW2 cannot be believable.
15. Having considered the submissions, on meaningful reading of evidence of PW2 as a whole, one gets an impression that evidence of PW2 is very natural and specific on material terms.
PW2 in his cross examination stated that he had accompanied the deceased Rahul and left MACT No.395/2022 by SHELENDER Page 5 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK
Date: 2024.09.13 16:39:16 +0530 together towards Rahul's in laws house.
PW2 further stated that Rahul was on his motorcycle and he was on another motorcycle and distance between their motorcycles was around 20 meters, at the time of accident.
PW2 further gave the details about the place of accident and also stated that after the accident deceased Rahul received injury on his head.
PW2 states that after the accident he called father of deceased and his wife and he reached at Rama Hospital at 11/12 midnight.
PW2 further states that police had taken his statement regarding the accident and accident occurred due to negligent driving of offending vehicle no.UK-06CB-3469.
Thus, nothing came in the cross examination to disbelieve the version of PW2.
So far as the question that name of PW2 is not mentioned in the list of witnesses, does not to the opinion of this Tribunal affect the evidence of PW2.

PW2 has stated that his statement was recorded by the police, merely because that the police did not mention his name in the list of witnesses, does not establish that he was not eye witness when otherwise his evidence is believable and consistent on material aspects.

16. Evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from police documents also as the site plan prepared by the IO also mentions the place where the accident occurred and offending vehicle struck the motorcycle of deceased from behind.
No doubt in the mechanical inspection report of offending truck prepared during the investigation of the criminal case mentions that rear bumper of the truck was damaged.

Such mechanical inspection report no doubt contradicts the version of the accident but at the same time it be noted that merely because mechanical inspection report mentions rear portion of the truck being damaged, it cannot be stated that accident had not occurred from the vehicle in question no.UK-06CB-3469.

This Tribunal has already concluded that evidence of PW2/eye witness is worthy MACT No.395/2022 by SHELENDER SHELENDER MALIK Page 6 MALIK Date: 2024.09.13 16:39:25 +0530 of reliance in the manner in which accident occurred.

Mechanical inspection report cannot be preferred to the consistent and cogent evidence of PW2, more particularly when same has not been put to the witness nor any IO of the case has been examined to clarify on this aspect.
It is quite possible that due to clerical mistake it might have been mentioned that rear portion of the truck is damaged.
Therefore this aspect does not affect the very credible evidence of PW2.

sentences.text: important aspect to note that after the accident offending truck no.UK-06CB-3469 was present at the place of accident and driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended immediately after the accident.
17. Respondent no.1/driver never appeared in the witness box nor even sought to be summoned by insurance company to prove if there was any other version regarding the accident.

Delay in FIR has no relevance at all in the peculiar circumstances of the case as it is stated in the FIR itself that offending truck and its driver was apprehended at the spot after the accident however on account of unfortunate death of a young boy, parents came forward to the police to lodge the FIR after about eight days.
Therefore such delay has no relevance regarding the issue under consideration.
As such it is concluded that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle/ truck no.UK-06CB-3469.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners.
Issue No.2 18.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award MACT No.395/2022 by SHELENDER Page 7 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.09.13 16:39:32 +0530 determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 19.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Rahul Kumar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.

Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under MACT No.395/2022 Digitally signed Page 9 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.09.13 16:39:44 +0530
the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

20. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased 21.
Petitioner no.1/PW1 Kajal (widow of the deceased) in her evidence deposed that her deceased husband was 25 years of age at the time of accident and his date of birth was 16.04.1997.
To prove this fact, PW1 has proved copy of Aadhar card of deceased as Ex.PW1/4 wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned to be 16.04.1997.
This documents in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of his death due to accident (31.03.2022) was 24 years.
Assessment of Income of deceased 22.

PW1 Ms.Kajal, widow of the deceased has testified that at the time of accident her deceased husband was working as House Keeping with Eagle Eye, Security & House Keeping Services and he was getting monthly salary of Rs.18,000/-.
PW1 has proved identity card issued by Eagle Eye Security & House Keeping Services as Ex.PW1/5.

However it is matter of record that petitioners are residents of Delhi.
Aadhar cards of petitioners as well as deceased Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/4 bear address of Delhi.
In such circumstances this Tribunal assesses notional income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi i.e. Rs.16,064/- per month.

An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.

Future Prospects 25.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

26. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 24 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
29.

In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

In view of pronouncement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra) and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others 2018 ACJ 2782 compensation awardable under conventional heads, namely, loss to estate,
loss of consortium and funeral expenses are to be MACT No.395/2022 SHELENDER SHELENDER MALIK Page 13 MALIK Date: 2024.09.13 16:40:07 +0530 enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 18.10.2023 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle/truck no.UK-06CB-3469 on 31.03.2022 at 11.00 pm at near Chijarshi Toll Tax within the jurisdiction of PS Pilakhua, District Hapur, UP in a rash and negligent manner and Kajal And Ors vs Firasat Ali And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102422473/
2 caused the death of deceased Sh.Rahul Kumar?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. No evidence has been led on behalf of either respondent no.1 and 2 or on behalf of R3/insurance company.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
PW2 has stated that his statement was recorded by the police, merely because that the police did not mention his name in the list of witnesses, does not establish that he was not eye witness when otherwise his evidence is believable and consistent on material aspects.
Such mechanical inspection report no doubt contradicts the version of the accident but at the same time it be noted that merely because mechanical inspection report mentions rear portion of the truck being damaged, it cannot be stated that accident had not occurred from the vehicle in question no.UK-06CB-3469.
Mechanical inspection report cannot be preferred to the consistent and cogent evidence of PW2, more particularly when same has not been put to the witness nor any IO of the case has been examined to clarify on this aspect.
Delay in FIR has no relevance at all in the peculiar circumstances of the case as it is stated in the FIR itself that offending truck and its driver was apprehended at the spot after the accident however on account of unfortunate death of a young boy, parents came forward to the police to lodge the FIR after about eight days.
Therefore such delay has no relevance regarding the issue under consideration.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 19.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of his death due to accident (31.03.2022) was 24 years.
Assessment of Income of deceased 22.
In such circumstances this Tribunal assesses notional income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi i.e. Rs.16,064/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 23.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as MACT No.395/2022 by SHELENDER Page 12 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.09.13 16:40:02 +0530 Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
